title: Prefill Latency Buffer and Kernel Prober: reduce tail for mixed streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: design and ship an admission + shaping subsystem that reduces p95/p99 prefill+decode tail latency for mixed-length request streams while preserving throughput. We will introduce a small on-node prefetched "latency buffer" for short low-token requests and a kernel-probing score to select compact vs wide kernels dynamically. This ticket covers design, prototype, benchmarks, safety checks, and staged rollout to production traffic bundles.
technical_solution: We propose two coordinated mechanisms: (1) Latency Buffer (LB): a lightweight per-GPU ring buffer that keeps a small cache of prefetched KV states and short-LLM micro-batches to immediately serve short requests without waiting for large batch coalescing. LB uses request-size and recent inter-arrival statistics to decide residency and eviction. (2) Kernel Prober Score (KPS): an online scoring function that experiments with alternative kernel codepaths (compact / wide / quantized-friendly) by periodically probing with low-priority shadow workloads and measuring real decode latency per-token and end-to-end tail. KPS feeds the admission controller and the batch shaper so they can choose to route a given request to a kernel variant with better tail behavior. Admission controller changes: integrate size-aware fast-path for LB, allow speculative allocation of tiny decode slots with strict deadline enforcement, and add backpressure signals to avoid starvation of long-running batches. We also add attention-prefetch hints during prefill to prioritize KV warming for sequences likely to decode quickly.
metrics: primary: p99 prefill+decode latency under 95th percentile traffic <= baseline * 0.7
throughput: sustained token/sec within 5% of baseline under same cluster load
safeguard: no regression in correctness or increased error rates for structured outputs
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark harness shows >=20% reduction in measured p99 for mixed short+long workload (realistic production trace) on staging cluster
End-to-end integration tests pass with LB disabled/enabled toggles and deterministic fallback to baseline kernel path
KPS warmup probe does not increase tail latency for steady-state heavy workloads (verified via chaos tests)
Feature flagged rollout plan with canary traffic threshold and automatic rollback when p99 > baseline * 1.1
Observability: dashboards with KPS scores, LB occupancy, admission reject rate, and per-kernel latencies deployed to Console release runtime-2026.03

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Latency Buffer increases tail for long-running batches by shifting kernels away. Mitigation: make LB opt-in per-tenant and enforce strict hard-deadlines with fallback and telemetry to detect shift; add traffic-weighted canaries.

Risk: KPS probes add noise and can mislead kernel selection. Mitigation: use low-priority probes that run in isolated lane, aggregate over windows and require statistically significant delta before switching.
Risk: Increased GPU memory pressure due to cached KV/prefetch. Mitigation: adaptive LB sizing, eviction policy by LRU+cost, and OOM circuit-breaker to demote LB entries.
Risk: Observability blind spots. Mitigation: add pre-deployment dashboards and anomaly detectors; instrument both shadow and live measurements.
Risk: Customer-facing regressions. Mitigation: gradual rollout per-tenant with automatic rollback triggers and ability to pin kernel version per-route.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: stage 0 - internal perf lab (unit + integration) -> stage 1 - staging cluster with production trace replay -> stage 2 - 1% prod traffic canary for latency-sensitive tenants -> stage 3 - 25% traffic, monitor 48h -> stage 4 - full rollout. Rollback triggers: p99 regression >10% for canaryed tenants or error rate spike >2x.
